messages:
Priya (Support): FYI escalation from AcmePay — they've reported a sudden p99 spike on /v1/generate in us-west-2. p95 sits ~450ms but p99 jumped from ~800ms to ~3.2s starting ~17:30 UTC. Customer impact: interactive chat timeouts. Request id: req_8b9f2c.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Thanks. Any recent deploys or config changes? Also need sample request headers + model name.
Priya (Support): They included this in the ticket: model: redwood-7b-instruct (quantized), region: us-west-2, API key masked (starts with ak_Acme...). No deploys on our side reported in that timeframe. They attached a minimal repro curl.
Priya (Support): Repro example they provided:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ak_AcmeXXXX' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-instruct","input":"summarize: long text...","max_tokens":512}'
```
Dan (Oncall SRE): Opening the incident timeline. @auto-inc-bot can you pull the traces for req_8b9f2c and surface top spans?
auto-inc-bot: Traces queued. Found 12 traces matching tag: req_8b9f2c, start_time 1769455800-1769457000. High tail observed on runtime token loop + disk swap on node gpu-11.
Leo (Infra): Disk swap? Which node pool? I see GPU host gpu-11 (p-xl) had a memory pressure event at 17:29:45 UTC, kernel OOM killer invoked for process `kv-cache-service`. That correlates.
Maya (Eng-Platform): Hmm. We recently enabled larger KV cache persistence for the quantized path in us-west-2 canary (policy id: kvp-2026-03). Could be interacting with memory footprint causing eviction and swapping.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Immediate mitigations — list of actionable items: 1) Route AcmePay traffic to fallback model variant in another region. 2) Apply emergency rate cap for their API key. 3) Rollback the KV persistence canary in us-west-2 or reduce cache size. Who can do each?
Leo (Infra): I can route and apply rate cap. Quick command to limit their key to 8 rps: 
```bash
# admin API (internal)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/admin/keys/ak_AcmeXXXX/limits \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"rate_limit_rps":8}'
```
Leo (Infra): I've set a temporary cap and confirmed 200 OK.
Maya (Eng-Platform): I can flip the routing. Suggest fallback to `redwood-3b-latency` in us-east-1 (lower mem footprint). Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl route set --customer acmepay --model redwood-3b-latency --region us-east-1 --reason "p99 emergency fallback"
```
Maya (Eng-Platform): Done — traffic shift started, ~40% diverted in first 2m.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Good. Also, toggle guardrail to enable circuit breaker for the quantized runtime pool to avoid full-node swap. Add ephemeral `circuit-breaker: true` label to pool p-xl-usw2.
Maya (Eng-Platform): Applying circuit breaker config now. Patch: `platform-config/pools/p-xl-usw2.json` updated to `max_inflight_per_node=12` and `circuit_breaker_enabled=true`. Deployed.
Priya (Support): Customer reports immediate improvement: interactive latency back down, some requests still p99 ~1.1s but much better. Thank you. They're asking: what caused it and what will we do to prevent this happening again?
Dan (Oncall SRE): Root cause summary (initial): 1) KV cache persistence change increased resident memory on the quantized runtime in canary hosts. 2) Under steady higher token lengths from AcmePay, memory pressure led to swap/OOM on gpu-11, causing token loop stalls and huge tail latencies. 3) Lack of an aggressive per-customer token-rate limiter + no automatic fallback circuit on pool-level allowed sustained overload.
Leo (Infra): Note: our node autoscaler didn't spin up new nodes because the metric used was GPU compute, not host memory. So memory pressure wasn't accounted. Need to adjust autoscaler policy.
Maya (Eng-Platform): Proposed mitigations (short, mid, long):
- Short (minutes): route heavy customers to fallback models/regions; apply emergency per-key rate limits; enable pool circuit breaker.
- Mid (hours): rollback KV persistence canary; reconfigure autoscaler to consider host memory pressure; add token-based throttles (tokens/sec) per key.
- Long (weeks): implement runtime-level circuit breakers that detect rising swap and proactively reject/redirect, integrate model variants in routing policy, and add a booking system for large token bursts.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Add SLO guardrails we should enforce: p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1.2s for interactive tier in region; per-customer token-rate limit default 50k tokens/day and burst cap 2000 tokens/min (configurable per plan); automatic fallback when 3 consecutive p99 breaches in 10m.
Priya (Support): I'll update the customer with the short-term mitigation timeline and CC product. Also creating a support ticket INC-2026-3348 and linking this thread.
Maya (Eng-Platform): I'll open infra ticket to change autoscaler: TICKET-PLAT-986 (autoscaler: include host_mem_used metric).
Leo (Infra): I'll follow up on node health and replace gpu-11; OOB replacement scheduled.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Action items (owners):
- Leo: confirm replacement and retrospective on gpu-11 (due EOD).
- Maya: rollback canary + autoscaler change (due 3h).
- Platform/Runtime: design runtime circuit breaker and add token-based throttles (spec draft due 5 business days).
- Priya: customer comms + confirm satisfaction (within 1h).
Dan (Oncall SRE): Also adjust alerts: add a synthetic p99 probe for representative workloads per region and fire automated job to activate fallback if p99 > 1.2s for 5m.
Priya (Support): AcmePay replied: "Thanks, latency is better. Please keep us posted." Marking customer as responding.
auto-inc-bot: Incident INC-2026-3348 created and linked to traces/metrics/this-thread.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Closing loop for now — keeping thread open for post-mortem notes. We'll schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow with Platform + Runtime + Infra + Support.
Priya (Support): Noted. Adding postmortem invite.
Maya (Eng-Platform): Quick follow-up note for runbook improvements: include operator commands to route a single customer's traffic across models and regions and ensure token-rate-limiter admin endpoints are documented. I'll add to runbook repo.
Dan (Oncall SRE): Thanks all. If anyone observes regression reappear, @channel escalate and re-open.
